articles.title: The Past, Present, and Future of Persona with P-Studio Head Kazuhisa Wada | IGN30 Interview
articles.summary: From Persona 3 saving Atlus to empowering younger developers, Wada-san tells us his story of coming up through the ranks and leading the Persona series.
body: From Persona 2: Eternal Punishment to the upcoming Persona 6, creative producer and chief director of P-Studio with Atlus Kazuhisa Wada has had a hand in shaping the spinoff-turned-mainline series. And with the career spanning over 30 years, we're excited to see how he and his team continue to shape the beloved RPG series. As part of our IGN30 series where we have open conversations with storied developers about their careers from the early days to where they are today, I talked with Wada-san and he shared anecdotes of coming up through Atlus' ranks and what he envisions for the future of the franchise.
This interview was conducted with Sega interpreter Gavin Green and was edited for clarity and readability. You can watch the video version of this interview above.

articles.title: GTA 6’s Criminal Profile Isn’t a Morality Spectrum – It’s an RPG Class System
articles.summary: Doing violent crimes changes your criminal profile in GTA 6, but this isn't a punishment for being "evil" - it's a new take on the RPG class system.
body: This is an opinion piece from writer Samuel Horti. IGN's opinion columns represent the personal viewpoints of the writer, drawing on their own experiences and research to explore the exciting world of video games.

GTA 6 is a tender love story about a couple clinging to each other through chaos, about the impossible lengths people go for their families, about second chances and forgiveness, about the small moments of romance – watching TV entwined on the sofa, holding hands on the beach, an unexpected compliment – in which relationships bloom.
It is also a game where you can grab a bystander with a digger's claw and squeeze until their head pops.

Modern GTA games have sometimes struggled to square attempts at serious protagonists, or at least protagonists with any depth or humanity, with their inevitable open-world crime sprees. It's hard to take a potentially poignant cut-scene seriously when you've just mowed down 25 pedestrians with a machine gun, and pelted another dozen with RPGs.
points: Doing violent crimes changes your criminal profile in GTA 6, but this isn't a punishment for being "evil" - it's a new take on the RPG class system.

articles.title: So, Did GTA 6 Live up to the Hype?
articles.summary: Thirteen years — that’s how long players waited to get their hands on Grand Theft Auto 6. The road to Rockstar’s mega-hit was an unusually long one for a bankable franchise video game, but the wait was arguably an even better marketing tactic than that flashy Netflix reveal.
body: While that helped GTA 6 ’s launch reach the loudest crescendo possible, it came with a risk. Too much excitement can be a bad thing. Rockstar Games would have to combat outsized expectations from fans who had convinced themselves that the open-world game would feature a bevy of revolutionary features, regardless of how implausible they were.
Now that the dust has settled and players are cruising around Leonida, I find myself trying to unpack an impossible question: Did GTA 6 live up to all that hype, after all?

On some level, it’s a ridiculous thing to ask. Hype is not a quantifiable metric, so how would you even begin to measure how well it paid off? I suppose we could start by looking at sales data. We already know GTA 6 is a hit in that regard, as Rockstar confirmed that it sold 32.5 million copies in its pre-release period alone. That’s a fairly convincing $3.79 billion answer, right? But there was never any doubt that GTA 6 would be a financial success. If anything, the pre-release sales are actually a reflection of the hype, not the game itself. It’s going to take a few more rounds of post-launch sales figures to gauge success by numbers.

articles.title: Everything Coming to Netflix in December 2026
articles.summary: For December, Netflix has decided to onboard all the Shreks, Brad Pitt returning as Cliff Booth, and a new Pride and Prejudice adaptation. But that's not all!
body: Netflix is closing out 2026 with a stacked December full of all four Shreks, two Now You See Mes, Longlegs, all six seasons of 2 Broke Girls, and — of course — the latest David Fincher movie, which just so happens to be a spin-off/sequel to Quentin Tarantino's Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.

Yes, Brad Pitt is back in the role that garnered him an Oscar, stuntman Cliff Booth, in The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. The film was written by Tarantino himself, though Fincher took over the directing duties so Tarantino could still stick to his "I'm only directing 10 movies" career goal.

There's also Brad (The Incredibles, Mission: Impossible - Ghost Protocol) Bird's new animated movie, Ray Gunn, a fresh Pride and Prejudice adaptation, a JonBenét Ramsey true crime series starring Melissa McCarthy, a new comedy starring Cameron Diaz, and much more!
If you're just looking for a detailed list of everything coming to Netflix in December, you can jump to the full release schedule by day.

body: This is the version of Monopoly I own, albeit a newer edition of the game. It's just classic Monopoly. But as I've come to realize over the years of writing commerce content, there's never just one Monopoly on sale at any given time.

Monopoly is like the Fortnite of video games. There's crossovers for pretty much every major franchise out there. In fact, it's hard to find a franchise that Hasbro hasn't given the "Fast-paced Real Estate Trading Game" treatment to. There's even a Supernatural Monopoly Edition where you can play as Sam or Dean. It's a wild world out there.

Anyway, my point is, there are actually a number of reskinned versions of Monopoly on sale right now too. All of these editions are more expensive than the base game and feature unique elements from whatever franchise they are tied to. If you want a different spin on Monopoly, you've got options.

articles.title: Xbox players Angry They Aren't Getting The Next Official Yooka-Laylee Release
articles.summary: Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition is skipping Microsoft's gaming platforms, and Xbox players aren't happy because Playtonic has typically released games in this Banjo-Kazooie spiritual successor series on Xbox consoles.
body: Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition was announced on Nov. 25 and is a current-gen upgrade for the 2019 platformer. While the first Yooka-Laylee game emulated the feel of Banjo-Kazooie, Impossible Lair draws inspiration from Rare's work on the Donkey Kong Country series. Its Definitive Edition will launch on Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Windows PC on Dec. 15, and it will vastly improve the lighting, textures, frame rate, and resolution.

While Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair came out on Xbox One in 2019, an Xbox Series X or S version of the Definitive Edition wasn't part of the initial announcement. Players asked Playtonic about this, so the developer took to X to explain why it wasn't coming to the console. "We've had to prioritise our efforts given the technical challenges and costs presented in the creation of this updated version of the game and as a result, we are unable to commit to any additional platforms for the foreseeable future," Playtonic explained, admitting later in the statement that "the cost of bringing it to more platforms just isn't viable for us at this time."

articles.title: 007 First Light's Brilliant Tutorial Is a Game Direction Miracle
articles.summary: The 007 First Light tutorial is the platonic ideal of a perfect video game tutorial. IO Interactive reveals how it came together.
body: How did James Bond become James Bond? Through a 1980s movie montage, of course! Come on. Everyone knows that one.

007 First Light, IO Interactive’s 2026 take on James Bond and the greatest 007 game of the century (so far), did a whole lot of shaking up. It’s billed as an origin story for Ian Fleming’s famous spy, coloring in the background of a character often wrapped in intrigue. It’s also IO Interactive’s first foray outside of the Hitman-iverse in 16 years, allowing the studio ample room to flex its action chops. But as we approach the end of the year — with all of the reflection and end-of-year debates that incurs — 007 First Light perhaps stands out most for one innovation: its killer tutorial.

“It was maybe also one of the hardest tutorials in gaming history, I could imagine. I don't know. I'm not gonna speak for others, but it was so hard,” Hakan Abrak, game director on 007 First Ligh t, told Polygon in an interview. “And you know, we were nervous whether it's gonna work out, because who wants to be in a tutorial for such a long time, right?”
points: The 007 First Light tutorial is the platonic ideal of a perfect video game tutorial.

articles.title: ArcheAge Chronicles developer XL Games faces major layoffs and possible closure after disappointing sales
articles.summary: XL Games, the South Korean studio behind ArcheAge Chronicles, is planning a major restructuring and has not ruled out closing altogether after the game failed to meet sales expectations.
body: As reported by Korean outlet Money Today Broadcasting (MTN), translated by machine, CEO Choi Kwan-ho told staff in a letter on 26th November that the company would first ask for voluntary redundancies before moving on to compulsory layoffs.

"Criticisms regarding ArcheAge Chronicles' lack of polish despite its long development period, as well as complaints concerning bugs, gameplay, and optimisation, continue to persist," Choi wrote, according to MTN. "Sales are also showing a downward trend, and we anticipate revenue that will fall far short of expectations."
Choi said XL Games will try to address some of those problems in a December update, to see whether that turns things around.
"However, the company is currently at a critical crossroads where we must even consider the possibility of going out of business," he added.
points: XL Games, the South Korean studio behind ArcheAge Chronicles, is planning a major restructuring and has not ruled out closing altogether after the game failed to meet sales expectations.

articles.title: Marvel Snap's Black Friday Deal Went Terribly Wrong
articles.summary: Marvel Snap players had been saving up for Black Friday deals on Collector's Packs that could net them new cards. When the daily reset that was supposed to kick off the discount finally rolled around, though, something went wrong.
body: Card acquisition is expensive in Marvel Snap. The cheapest way to get new Series 5 cards — the highest series tier most competitive new card releases fall under — is to spend 4,000 Collector's Tokens for a Series 5 Collector's Pack that will randomly snag the player an older Series 5 card they don't own. Collector's Tokens are earned slowly in-game or bought with Gold, Marvel Snap's premium currency.

As a result, players look for discounts or cheaper ways to get new cards. After last week's update, Marvel Snap dataminers discovered a planned discount on standard Collector's Packs for Black Friday. During this deal, players were supposed to be able to buy up to five Series 5 packs for just 3,200 Collector's Tokens per pack (Series 3 and 4 packs would also be discounted). While it was only a 20% discount, this was still going to be a great deal for those who stockpiled tokens and could speed up their journey to becoming collection-complete.

Pop back every weekend to find out what Jeremy, Josh, Rick and Ted have become obsessed with this time, whether it's the canon height of Thief's Garrett or that time someone in the Vatican pirated Football Manager.

articles.title: A game of cards that could change the world - All Will Rise appeals because it's unafraid to have a perspective
articles.summary: I'm a big fan of the moment when, years into a gaming subgenre's existence, people start rethinking what those games are capable of. All the expected ideas, they've been done, so the latecomers are by necessity inventors if they want to stand out. All Will Rise is one of them.
body: Made by Speculative Agency, and touting star-quality talent like award-winning writer and narrative designer Meghna Jayanth (80 Days, Sable, Thirsty Suitors ), All Will Rise follows hot-shot and sometimes hot-headed lawyer Kuyili in her battle against greedy corporations, which are inadvertently - or perhaps deliberately - destroying the natural world around them. In this case they've literally and quite spectacularly set a river on fire. There's out-of-court action as you build a case against someone - read: build your deck of cards to use against them - then there's courtroom action as you deploy your card-claims and make your winning arguments.

articles.title: Team Ninja producer says the Nioh studio uses AI 'to streamline certain workflows', but insists 'deciding how to craft the game and what makes it enjoyable must be done by humans'
articles.summary: Team Ninja producer Kohei Shibata has revealed that the studio behind Nioh and Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty uses AI in its development processes. But he stressed that games should still ultimately be crafted by humans.
body: Speaking to INVEN Global at South Korea's CGON 2026 (via Eurogamer ), Shibata said that the studio uses "AI in QA and various verification tasks to streamline certain workflows."

Shibata argued that if AI can "shorten task times" then developers can focus their efforts on "elevating the game's overall quality," although he caveated that "since it's still a new technology, we are continuously evaluating the most appropriate ways to implement it."

One thing Shibata emphasises, however, is that the quality of a game still rests upon human-centred design. "What matters fundamentally is that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands. Repetitive, simple tasks that anyone must perform can be streamlined by technology. But ultimately, deciding how to craft the game and what makes it enjoyable must be done by humans."
He also pointed out that "using AI itself should never become the goal. I believe the principle that humans must think for themselves and finish the game will remain unchanged in the future."
points: Team Ninja producer Kohei Shibata has revealed that the studio behind Nioh and Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty uses AI in its development processes.

articles.title: What we've been playing - "It is 2014 and a woman on a bus calls me disgusting and a charlatan"
articles.summary: It's nearly December. In fact, it will be next week. How do you feel about that? I'm undecided and I also have cold feet. But enough of that, welcome back to our regular feature where we say a bit about the games we've been playing this week!
body: But forget about us, what about you? What have you been playing this week? Let us know below. And don't forget that we have an entire archive of previous What We've Been Playings for your perusal should you want to know what you were playing week, month, or even a year ago.

I've mostly been playing GTA 6 and I really like it. What I've been most surprised by is the game's maturity, which seems like an odd thing to say when people are having things rammed up their wotsits, and there's so much deliberately stupid and slapstick stuff happening. But there's another level that exists primarily between Jason and Lucia. It's evident in moments such as helping Lucia build flatpack furniture, then watching a montage of tender moments around that flatpack furniture, which looked a lot like life, like actual life, to me. Two people doing life together, existing, overlapping. I don't know that we've ever seen a relationship in so much detail before. It's really impressive.

articles.title: A purported remake of The Simpsons: Hit & Run may have been scrapped, after a developer says their project was part of 'a gaggle of cancellations'
articles.summary: Earlier this year, rumours began to circulate that a remake of The Simpsons: Hit & Run was in the works, rumours which were lent further credence after Simpsons creator Matt Groening implied that a return of the PS2-era GTA clone was on the cards.
body: On LinkedIn (via Eurogamer ) game designer Darren Evenson announced that he had been let go from New Radical Games, a studio formed from the ashes of Radical Entertainment, which developed The Simpsons: Hit & Run as well as the open-world superhero game Prototype. New Radical was rumoured to be working on a redux of Hit & Run, but it seems that, if that was indeed the case, it no longer is.

"It seems that not even a fantastic project with an incredible team is immune from the current state of the industry right now, as what we were working on at New Radical Games (although mind blowingly awesome) was part of a whole gaggle of cancellations. A gaggle I say!" Evenson wrote. He then added: "Oh you silly suits with spreadsheets… will you EVER learn? If you don't make the game, you can't make the money…and if you don't make the money then you don't get the power…and… well, there's more to that quote, but I digress."

articles.title: Queen's Domain review: The finest metroidvania ever made
articles.summary: 50 hours, four endings, and 52 achievements of pure videogames.
body: Metroidvania is an annoying genre name, but it's useful. A Metroid-type game, with a little 'vania for the fellas: Platform around an open-ended, vertically-oriented world. When you hit a wall, go somewhere else until you unlock a movement-centric powerup to open new pathways. They call 'em "search-action" games in Japan, and that's a way better name.

They're mostly 2D. Metroid Prime did it 3D-style and it's an all-time classic. Dark Souls 1 had the dense, vertical, interconnected world, but not the movement stuff, so let's say it doesn't count as a genre-mate. Queen's Domain is the best game of this style I have ever played, 2D or 3D. Hollow Knight, Symphony of the Night, Metroid Prime⁠—I love 'em, but there's a new queen of the genre. After around 50 hours, four endings, all 52 achievements, and a lot of collectible hunting, I remain in awe of this game.
points: 50 hours, four endings, and 52 achievements of pure videogames.
